name: LinkedIn Profile Analysis - Backend Developer
description: Signals extracted from LinkedIn profiles to evidence Backend Developer skills. LinkedIn provides professional context, endorsements, recommendations, and career progression data.

sections.notes: Self-described; provides intent and specialization context (e.g., 'Senior Distributed Systems Engineer' vs generic 'Software Developer').

sections.description: Work experience entries with job titles, companies, and responsibilities.
sections.notes: Similar to CV work experience. Look for backend-specific titles and descriptions of data scale, throughput, and system reliability.
quality_indicators: Backend-specific job titles (Backend Engineer, Distributed Systems Engineer, API Platform Engineer, Data Infrastructure Developer)
Duration and continuity in backend roles
Company scale and domain complexity (fintech, e-commerce, high-throughput streaming)
Specific technologies, databases, and architectural patterns described

sections.description: Skills listed with endorsement counts from connections.
sections.notes: Endorsements have very low evidential value on their own. They provide a high-level self-reported technology inventory.
Theoretical domain indicator, not practical proof.

sections.description: Projects section with descriptions and links.
sections.notes: Provides additional project context. Links to live repositories or API docs increase strength.

sections.description: Written recommendations from engineering leads, architects, or peers.
sections.notes: Third-party validation of technical leadership, code quality, and incident response competency.

sections.description: Technical posts and articles published on LinkedIn.
sections.notes: Articles about backend architecture, database optimizations, or post-mortem analyses indicate deep systems grasp.

signal_mapping.description: How LinkedIn mentions map to skill evidence using COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}). AI should use these patterns.

patterns.pattern: LinkedIn skills endorsement for 'Redis' or 'Apache Kafka'
LinkedIn skills endorsement for 'Microservices' or 'REST APIs'
Job experience explicitly describing building high-throughput event-driven microservices
Job experience describing database optimization, indexing, and migration pipelines
Job experience describing authentication architecture (OAuth2, JWT, RBAC)
Job experience describing fault-tolerant resilience engineering (Circuit Breakers, Bulkheads)
Job experience describing application telemetry instrumentation (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus)
Technical article about distributed database consistency, Saga pattern, or CQRS

important_notes: ALL extracted signals MUST be mapped to COMPOSITE KEYS ({skill_id}.{subskill_id})
LinkedIn data supplements but should not override verified code or assessment evidence
Endorsements have near-zero evidential value on their own
Job titles can be inflated — cross-reference with actual system scale and architectural responsibilities described
Career trajectory (progression from junior bug fixing to mid feature ownership to senior platform/systems architecture) provides valuable context
Specialized technical content (post-mortems, distributed systems trade-offs) indicates advanced seniority
